snippet.title: "What Mongols Did to Captured Queens Was Far Worse Than Death"
snippet.description:
What Mongols Did to Captured Queens Was Far Worse Than Death

The Mongol Empire is remembered as the largest land empire in human history — but behind its conquests lies a fully documented reality about how it treated the royal women of the kingdoms it destroyed. In this documentary, we uncover the real, historically verified fates of queens, princesses, and empresses captured during the Mongol conquests, using primary sources like the Persian chronicles of Ata-Malik Juvaini and Rashid al-Din, the Chinese Yuan Shi, and the eyewitness account of Franciscan envoy John of Plano Carpini.

This is not myth. This is not legend. This is real Mongol Empire history — verified through Persian, Chinese, and European chronicles written during and immediately after the conquests.

🔍 In this video, you'll learn:
– The true fate of Terken Khatun, the powerful Khwarezmian queen mother
– What happened to the women of Baghdad's Abbasid Caliphate after 1258
– How royal marriages were used as tools of Mongol political control
– The extraordinary rise of Sorghaghtani Beki, mother of two Mongol emperors
– How Töregene Khatun ruled the entire Mongol Empire as regent

📚 Sources: Ata-Malik Juvaini's "Tarikh-i Jahangushay," Rashid al-Din's "Jami al-Tawarikh," the Yuan Shi, and the travel account of John of Plano Carpini.

snippet.description:
On May 6, 1937, the German airship Hindenburg arrived in New Jersey after crossing the Atlantic. As it descended for landing, flames suddenly erupted near the tail. In just 30 seconds, the massive airship was consumed by fire. Thirty-six people lost their lives. The horrifying event was captured on film and broadcast worldwide—making it one of the first disasters ever seen by millions.

💥 The Hindenburg crash ended the era of passenger airships and left a lasting scar in aviation history.

snippet.title: Britain’s Worst Defeat of WWI - Russia's Great Winter Victory
snippet.description:
🎥 Watch 300+ exclusive videos on ✔ youtube ► https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMmaBzfCCwZ2KqaBJjkj0fw/join and ✔ Patreon ► https://www.patreon.com/kingsandgenerals

Kings and Generals animated historical documentary series on modern warfare the Great War and the Ottoman history during the World War I. Previously we covered the Rise of the Ottoman Empire from the humble beginnings as a small Turkic Beylik to the Fall of Constantinople 1453 covering all the major battles including (https://youtu.be/TDLmsiqhgns) and the reign of Mehmet II (https://youtu.be/TbqMBfxtOTI). After the Ottoman victory at Gallipoli and Bulgaria’s entry into the First World War, Istanbul shifted troops across a vast empire to meet the challenges of 1916. In the frozen Caucasus, General Nikolai Yudenich launches a meticulously prepared Russian offensive against the supposedly impregnable fortress of Erzurum. Winter marches, surprise attacks, and brutal fighting for mountain forts shatter the Ottoman Third Army and send it reeling westward. But while the Ottomans lose Erzurum, they strike back elsewhere. In the Sinai desert, Kress von Kressenstein’s forces raid British outposts near Katia, exposing the vulnerability of the Suez Canal. Farther east, the siege of Kut becomes a catastrophe for the British Empire. Relief columns repeatedly smash against Ottoman trenches at Sheikh Sa’ad, the Wadi, Hanna, Dujaila, and Sannaiyat—suffering appalling losses as General Charles Townshend’s starving garrison waits in vain. This episode follows the Russian advance through Persia, the fall of Kut after 147 days, and the strategic consequences of Britain’s twin failures at Gallipoli and Mesopotamia. It is a story of snowbound assaults, desert raids, and one of the most devastating surrenders of the Great War. Across three fronts, commanders gamble men, artillery, supply lines, and imperial prestige at terrible human cost.

snippet.description:
When Alexander the Great died, his empire was torn apart by ambition.
From the ashes of his world rose the last Greek kings — proud heirs of a legend who had conquered the East.
But far to the west, another power was rising — colder, patient, and built for conquest.

From King Philip V to King Perseus, from the glory of Cynoscephalae to the destruction of Pydna, this was the moment when the dream of Greece met the discipline of Rome — and shattered.

Witness the fall of the Macedonian dynasty, the burning of Corinth, and the tragic end of the ancient Greek world.
A world that lost its freedom… yet conquered its conqueror through philosophy, art, and spirit.

“Rome conquered Greece with swords — but Greece conquered Rome with ideas.”

Experience the rise of Rome and the twilight of Greece in this cinematic retelling —
a story of ambition, pride, and the eternal struggle between power and legacy.

snippet.title: Crossing the Rubicon Caesar Declares War
snippet.description:
He had conquered Gaul, defeated a thousand tribes, and brought unimaginable wealth to Rome.
But when Gaius Julius Caesar returned home, his greatest enemy wasn’t across the mountains — it was in the Senate.

Betrayed, cornered, and declared an outlaw, Caesar faced a choice that would change the course of history:
submit… or fight for destiny.

On a cold winter night in 49 BC, he stood before the Rubicon River — the sacred boundary no Roman general could cross with an army.
One step forward meant rebellion.
One step back meant ruin.

He whispered the words that echoed through eternity:

“The die is cast.”

This is the moment the Roman Republic died and an empire was born.
A story of power, loyalty, and ambition — of a man who chose immortality over obedience.

⚔️ From the Senate’s betrayal to the silent march of the 13th Legion,
this cinematic retelling captures the night Rome changed forever.

snippet.title: Charlemagne’s Grandsons Lost Everything - Birth of France
snippet.description:
🎥 Watch 300+ exclusive videos on ✔ youtube ► https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMmaBzfCCwZ2KqaBJjkj0fw/join and ✔ Patreon ► https://www.patreon.com/kingsandgenerals

Kings and Generals animated historical documentary series on the history of medieval period and Franks continues with a video on how the Capetians took the Frankish crown. In 987, Hugh Capet was crowned King of the Franks in Reims, ending Carolingian rule in West Francia and beginning a dynasty that would shape the future of France for centuries. But the Capetian rise was not a sudden coup. It was the result of generations of careful political survival, military service, marriage alliances, and opportunism. This video traces the story from the collapse of Charlemagne’s empire after the death of Louis the Pious to the Treaty of Verdun, the weakening of royal authority, and the rise of powerful regional magnates. Among them were the Robertians, ancestors of the Capetians, whose fortunes began with Robert the Strong and grew through the heroic defence of Paris by Odo against the Vikings. As Carolingian kings struggled to control West Francia, Robertian leaders became kingmakers, rivals, and sometimes kings themselves. Hugh the Great refused the throne, while his son Hugh Capet slowly built the alliances that would make his election possible. When Louis V died in 987, Hugh emerged as the safest candidate for nobles, clergy, and Ottonian power alike — founding the Capetian dynasty.
